# Roster — Design

The voices this guide draws on, ranked by how much design material each has in the BuildFeed corpus. Lanes covered: Visual craft and taste, Design process and working with teams, Design systems, Research and usability, Design career and practice.

## Figma
- Known for: The official Figma channel spotlighting how design tools, plugins, and AI agents evolve to support real product teams.
- Stance: It frames design as an increasingly automated, agent-assisted craft where documentation, motion, and system workflows get streamlined by built-in AI features. It also draws on outside creative fields to show how physical and editorial inspiration can enrich digital interface thinking.
- Channel: [Figma](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCQsVmhSa4X-G3lHlUtejzLA) · 65 videos in the corpus

## The Futur
- Known for: A business-of-design channel focused on turning creative skill into sustainable income through branding, positioning, and client strategy.
- Stance: It insists that visual polish alone never grows a business—clarity of offer, niche specialization, and authentic personal branding matter more. The angle is entrepreneurial: creatives are coached to price for value, define ideal clients, and build trust-based systems rather than chase ads or vanity metrics.
- Channel: [The Futur](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC-b3c7kxa5vU-bnmaROgvog) · 28 videos in the corpus

## Dive Club
- Known for: Interviews with in-house product designers unpacking how AI tools are reshaping the practice of building software interfaces.
- Stance: It treats AI as a collaborator or 'junior designer' that should extend human judgment and curiosity rather than replace creative thinking. The recurring theme is that taste, iteration habits, and interaction design instincts remain the real bottleneck even as AI collapses build times.
- Channel: [Dive Club](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCkCnraWwlnBw1_i7C9-3p0w) · 28 videos in the corpus

## Designer Tom
- Known for: Commentary on design culture, branding controversies, and how AI is reshaping creative direction and team workflows.
- Stance: It argues that bold, even polarizing design choices often outperform safe minimalism, and that AI is best used as a learnable creative tool rather than a magic replacement for authorship. The channel pushes teams to rethink workflows from scratch instead of just bolting AI onto old processes.
- Channel: [Designer Tom](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC4_qP33t3TGpEM0-96WfC6Q) · 26 videos in the corpus

## Lukas Margerie
- Known for: Hands-on tutorials showing how to chain AI design and coding tools into fast, production-ready workflows.
- Stance: It's relentlessly practical, treating AI generators as raw starting points that need pairing with design systems, MCPs, or component libraries to avoid generic output. The angle is speed and automation—turning prospecting, prototyping, and design iteration into repeatable, scalable routines.
- Channel: [Lukas Margerie](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCIZmRlV_wjS8jFQTbRxCV4g) · 22 videos in the corpus

## Sneak Peek Design

- Stance: It emphasizes that tool choice matters less than process—structured feedback loops, discovery work, and minimal meetings are what let teams ship faster with AI. # Positions — Design

Recurring stances across the roster. Each is a paraphrase; the links open the video at the moment the case is made.

## Visual craft and taste

### 1. Typography is the foundational craft skill; designers should master it before anything else.
- The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=137)
- Tommy Smith — [Tommy Smith - How side projects can land you a dream job](https://youtu.be/TYUC5Bs5HvQ?t=1988)

### 2. Keep font sizes and weights consistent so hierarchy reads cleanly instead of feeling discordant.
- Tommy Smith — [Tommy Smith - How side projects can land you a dream job](https://youtu.be/TYUC5Bs5HvQ?t=2013)
- Sneak Peek Design — [This is how I do Agentic Design at Mercury](https://youtu.be/io54c7ddCgw?t=2255)

### 3. Judgment develops by deliberately studying and collecting reference work from admired designers and products.
- The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=164)
- Sneak Peek Design — [This is how I do Agentic Design at Mercury](https://youtu.be/io54c7ddCgw?t=1060)

### 4. Copying and tracing admired work, if disclosed, is a legitimate early stage for building craft.
- The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=246)

### 5. Don't chase a perfect typeface; commit to a small set of fonts you can control well.
- Brent David Freaney — [Death of the finished state ft. Brent David Freaney (Special Offer) | Config 2026](https://youtu.be/Yz03ERsfDDM?t=1646)

## Design process and working with teams

### 6. Engineering handoff is shifting from static Figma specs/redlines to sharing live, working code prototypes that engineers can fork and build on directly.

- Figma — [Release Notes 2026: February Edition | Figma](https://youtu.be/QJIgDWol5CE?t=954)
- Tommy Smith — [Tommy Smith - How side projects can land you a dream job](https://youtu.be/TYUC5Bs5HvQ?t=1044)
- Dive Club — [How Anthropic, Every, & Ramp design with AI](https://youtu.be/V-jd3v9P-Ps?t=157)

### 7. Design walkthroughs and case studies should open with user pain points and business context before showing screens, not lead with visuals.

- The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=900)

# Disagreements — Design

Live debates where the roster pulls in different directions. One link per side, at the moment the case is made.

## Visual craft and taste

### 1. Is visual taste mostly an innate eye, or a muscle that can be deliberately built?
- **Taste is an innate 'eye' that surfaces given opportunity, harder to instill than other craft skills.**
  - Cameron Worboys — [Cameron Worboys - Inside an AI-native design org](https://youtu.be/KH9GBasDTI8?t=1862)
- **Taste can be learned and must be actively fostered through practice, like training a muscle.**
  - Brandon Jacoby — [Brandon Jacoby - Seeing Taste vs. Creating Taste as a designer](https://youtu.be/RaKFP_DuqpA?t=1412)

### 2. Should portfolios minimize explanatory text in favor of visuals, or still demonstrate conceptual design thinking?
- **Viewers won't read text, so portfolios should lead with visuals and interactions, not explanation.**
  - Tommy Smith — [Tommy Smith - How side projects can land you a dream job](https://youtu.be/TYUC5Bs5HvQ?t=1845)
- **Designers must demonstrate conceptual design understanding, not just surface visuals, to prove real skill.**
  - The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=132)

### 3. Is deliberately copying master works the right training method, or should designers prioritize rule-breaking exploration?
- **Copying admired work, clearly labeled as such, is an acceptable way to build early craft.**
  - The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=248)
- **Designers should play, break rules, and explore rather than replicate existing approaches.**
  - Designer Tom — [Designer uses languages he can't read. Here's why](https://youtu.be/ocsWyiDRYNk?t=177)

## Design process and working with teams

### 4. For handoff and critique, is a live shared code prototype enough, or is structured static documentation (specs, redlines, saved process) still necessary?
- **Live, working prototypes are sufficient and more effective than static documentation for handoff and reviews.**
  - Sneak Peek Design — [12 Senior Designers Show Their Engineering Handoff Process](https://youtu.be/CYPeIjgIfOE?t=1678)
  - Dive Club — [The trick to AI prototyping with your design system](https://youtu.be/CqMZTg7L-wE?t=2017)
- **Structured specs and documented process are still needed for clarity and traceability, even with better tooling.**
  - Sneak Peek Design — [12 Senior Designers Show Their Engineering Handoff Process](https://youtu.be/CYPeIjgIfOE?t=70)
  - The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=925)

## Design systems

### 5. Should design-system documentation and handoff artifacts be maintained by agents, or does precision still require manual craft?
- **Train agents to write and keep updating documentation like Code Connect and change logs as the system evolves.**
  - Figma — [My agent army writes Code Connect | Dev Mindset](https://youtu.be/KhyLHeGpWFA?t=83)
- **Hand-built token-mapped components remain faster and more precise than automated annotation for conveying exact spacing values.**
  - Sneak Peek Design — [12 Senior Designers Show Their Engineering Handoff Process](https://youtu.be/CYPeIjgIfOE?t=141)

### 6. Should a design system prioritize enforced structural consistency or make room for one-of-one expressive variation?
- **Keep structure intact and shared quality bars so components stay predictable and teams stay aligned at scale.**
  - Figma — [Getting started with slots](https://youtu.be/fpc0cUt1y1M?t=7)
  - Sneak Peek Design — [This is how I do Agentic Design at Mercury](https://youtu.be/io54c7ddCgw?t=3246)
- **Favor expressive, brand-unique output over strict sameness, since uniform systems risk feeling commoditized to users.**
  - Cameron Worboys — [Cameron Worboys - Inside an AI-native design org](https://youtu.be/KH9GBasDTI8?t=2703)

## Research and usability

### 7. When users voice a specific feature request, should teams build exactly that or dig for the hidden problem behind it?
- **Directly honor detailed feedback from engaged, thoughtful users as a trusted resource for the roadmap.**
  - John Bai — [John Bai - The Grok Bot design journey](https://youtu.be/E-VxnQO73s4?t=2474)
- **Discount the literal feature request and instead question why the user wants it to find the real underlying need.**
  - Enrico Tartarotti — [Enrico Tartarotti - How did one person design and build all of this?](https://youtu.be/0-41r6ifA7c?t=2718)

### 8. Should validation come from rigorous, structured usability testing or from fast, informal building-and-fixing with users?
- **Run a scored, multi-week pilot with defined tasks and usability testing before committing to a tool or design.**
  - Sneak Peek Design — [How I do AI Prototyping as a Designer in Healthcare](https://youtu.be/Fc_C5s_PEB4?t=3243)
- **Ship a rough, informally built version fast, then fix discrepancies as real usage reveals problems.**
  - Dive Club — [The trick to AI prototyping with your design system](https://youtu.be/CqMZTg7L-wE?t=991)

## Design career and practice

### 9. Is the AI shift good or bad news for early-career designers right now?
- **It's a leveling moment where a strong portfolio can beat pedigree, favoring new entrants.**
  - Cameron Worboys — [Cameron Worboys - Inside an AI-native design org](https://youtu.be/KH9GBasDTI8?t=2283)
- **Entry-level openings are shrinking and the traditional career ladder into seniority is breaking.**
  - Designer Tom — [The New Design Portfolio (No Case Studies)](https://youtu.be/5s32uf2v6yY?t=415)

### 10. Should companies keep investing in junior hires or focus only on immediately productive senior ICs?
- **Earlier-career people without old habits can outproduce many mid/senior designers and deserve investment.**
  - Ben Blumenrose — [Ben Blumenrose: 50+ Design Teams Use AI. Most Are Doing It Wrong.](https://youtu.be/f5-D53i7W5o?t=919)
- **Short-term pressure is pushing companies to cut junior hiring since they can't afford training time.**
  - Daniel Wert — [Understanding Today’s Design Job Market (Figma’s New Study + Daniel Wert)](https://youtu.be/wI8cEXyPK7Y?t=1329)

# Frameworks & vocabulary — Design

Named models, rules of thumb and terms of art the roster uses.

## Visual craft and taste

### Make Interfaces Feel Better
A documented skill of ~16 named principles like concentric radius and optical alignment for polishing UI.
- Lukas Margerie — [New Codex Design Workflow Makes Codex Better Than Most Designers](https://youtu.be/CPg5UYbYLhA?t=233)

### Design Canon Reading List
A named set of typography and grid-system books used to systematically train visual judgment.
- The Futur — [How to Make $100K as a Graphic Designer](https://youtu.be/Zys3dt503Q4?t=152)

### Match Cut
A film-editing term applied to motion-graphic brand presentations that transition seamlessly between shots.
- Designer Tom — [AI just retired this design legend](https://youtu.be/PBfkpkVAQTQ?t=40)

### Craft Crit
A recurring team ritual where visual hierarchy and typography details are reviewed and refined together.
- Sneak Peek Design — [This is how I do Agentic Design at Mercury](https://youtu.be/io54c7ddCgw?t=2191)

## Design process and working with teams

### Code Connect
A Figma system linking design components directly to their underlying code so agents and engineers get precise, production-accurate context during handoff.
- Figma — [My agent army writes Code Connect | Dev Mindset](https://youtu.be/KhyLHeGpWFA?t=163)
- Sneak Peek Design — [How I use Figma MCP + Claude to Vibe Code at Intercom](https://youtu.be/_9OdGDjFrCw?t=5)

### Double Diamond
A two-phase divergent/convergent design process model, referenced to describe skipping early exploration and starting work in the build-focused second diamond.
- Dive Club — [The 2026 AI Design Field Report (tools, process, and what's working)](https://youtu.be/Y0n6F9VlLVc?t=444)

### Product Trio
A cross-functional grouping of design, product, and engineering that jointly frames the problem before design work starts.
- Sneak Peek Design — [How I do AI Prototyping as a Designer in Healthcare](https://youtu.be/Fc_C5s_PEB4?t=819)

## Design systems

### Slots
Figma component property converting a frame into a customizable content container, reducing detachment and easing system maintenance.
- Figma — [Getting started with slots](https://youtu.be/fpc0cUt1y1M?t=26)

### Variables
Named Figma primitive of reusable values (color, number, string, boolean) that let a system adapt across contexts and brands.
- Figma — [Variables for brand designers | Figma](https://youtu.be/E6opeuuTygs?t=54)

### Crazy Eights (AI remix)
Rapid-ideation exercise adapted so agents generate many variations to curate from, replacing manual sketch rounds.
- Designer Tom — [They Canceled Figma 4 Months Ago. Here's What They Use Now.](https://youtu.be/i2V8P2WY0X0?t=1899)

### Kill zone
Named practice of setting aside AI-generated prototypes that miss the mark, tracked as documented, non-wasted exploration.
- Sneak Peek Design — [How I do AI Prototyping as a Designer in Healthcare](https://youtu.be/Fc_C5s_PEB4?t=2022)

## Research and usability

### ICE scoring (Impact, Confidence, Effort)
A three-factor scoring method used to compare candidate tools objectively across teams before committing.
- Sneak Peek Design — [How I do AI Prototyping as a Designer in Healthcare](https://youtu.be/Fc_C5s_PEB4?t=3119)

### Norman Door
Named example of a poorly designed affordance where it's unclear whether to push or pull, used to teach predictable failure.
- Thomas Watkins — [The Next Decade of UX: Why Psychology Matters More Than Ever (Feat. Thomas Watkins) | EP 57](https://youtu.be/gLqGgw8Zlaw?t=317)

### Mapping the Gap
A named exercise for identifying where a client currently is versus where they want to be, in their own words.
- The Futur — [Easy Way to Get Clients Without Ads or Cold DM's - FREE 2 HOUR MASTERCLASS](https://youtu.be/dOZkAqR_2lA?t=2239)

### Six-Stage Purchase Awareness Journey
A named model of six phases a person moves through before making a considered purchase decision.
- The Futur — [Easy Way to Get Clients Without Ads or Cold DM's - FREE 2 HOUR MASTERCLASS](https://youtu.be/dOZkAqR_2lA?t=2349)

## Design career and practice

### Outcome-Oriented Design
A named design paradigm where designers define adaptable boundaries for AI-driven outcomes instead of fixed step-by-step interfaces.
- Nielsen Norman Group — [Outcome-Oriented Design: The Era of AI Design](https://youtu.be/orvtAMGBgPE?t=60)

### Design Sprint (Google Ventures model)
A named five-day collaborative process, now being compressed into short synchronous check-ins plus independent AI-assisted work.
- Hannah Hearth — [Hannah Hearth - Design Careers in the Age of AI](https://youtu.be/K9qdl3M5NgE?t=971)

### Ideal Client Profile (ICP)
A defined profile of the exact buyer a freelancer targets, used to shape offers and pricing.
- The Futur — [Who Told You to Be 'Affordable'? (Price Like This Instead)](https://youtu.be/LdPHurNaIec?t=53)

### Irresistible Offer
A packaged offer built around a buyer's dream outcome so compelling that saying no feels foolish.
- The Futur — [Who Told You to Be 'Affordable'? (Price Like This Instead)](https://youtu.be/LdPHurNaIec?t=38)

### AI-native / AI fluency
A term of art describing designers who default to AI tools as their first instinct, like reflexively searching online.
- Ben Blumenrose — [Ben Blumenrose: 50+ Design Teams Use AI. Most Are Doing It Wrong.](https://youtu.be/f5-D53i7W5o?t=869)
